problem_class.label: convex
problem_class.details: Unconstrained minimization of convex differentiable component functions on a complete real inner-product space; strong convexity is not required.
problem_class.evidence: LongTails/Setups/InterpolatedFiniteSum.lean: Public.E and its instances; spec.admissible, ConvexOn clause.

problem_class.label: finite_sum
problem_class.details: The objective is F(x) = (1/m) Σ_i f_i(x), with m ≥ 1.

oracle.label: exact_gradient
oracle.details: Only exact component gradients are supplied; function values and full gradients are not oracle replies. Each query counts as one oracle call.
oracle.evidence: LongTails/Setups/InterpolatedFiniteSum.lean: spec.Query and spec.Reply; LongTails/Template.lean: execute and Convergence.

oracle.label: component_gradient
oracle.details: A query (i,x) returns the exact gradient of f_i at x. Exactness holds for every call index and oracle seed; no oracle error or sampling dependence is imposed.

distinctive_assumptions.label: other
distinctive_assumptions.details: Interpolation: there exists a common global minimizer xstar of every component with ‖x0−xstar‖ ≤ R. Every component gradient is globally L-Lipschitz. The ambient space is an arbitrary real Hilbert space. Public information comprises E, m, L and x0; R and ε are hidden parameters. Validity requires L > 0, R ≥ 0 and ε > 0. The allowed algorithm is restricted by equality to cyclicGradient m L x0.
distinctive_assumptions.evidence: LongTails/Setups/InterpolatedFiniteSum.lean: Public, Params, spec.publicInput, spec.valid, spec.admissible and spec.allowedAlgorithm.

accuracy.label: objective_gap
accuracy.details: The output is one point x satisfying (1/m) Σ_i [f_i(x)−f_i(xstar)] ≤ ε for a common global minimizer xstar. No averaging requirement is stated in successful.

accuracy.label: almost_sure
accuracy.details: The ε objective-gap inequality must hold almost surely under the output law, rather than merely in expectation. The oracle-call budget is fixed and bounds calls for every seed.

setup_category.label: classical
setup_category.reason: Smooth convex finite-sum optimization with exact component gradients and interpolation is an established formulation. This setup states it in a real Hilbert space with an almost-sure objective-gap criterion.

descriptionHtml:
Cyclic Gradient Under Interpolation

We consider minimizing F(x)=m−1∑i=0m−1fi(x) on a real Hilbert space E, where m≥1 is an integer. Each component fi:E→R is convex and differentiable with an L-Lipschitz gradient, where L>0. The components share a global minimizer x⋆, and the given starting point x0∈E satisfies ∥x0−x⋆∥≤R for R≥0. The oracle returns ∇fi(x) at a queried pair (i,x). Cyclic gradient descent with step size 1/L must return its last iterate x¯ with F(x¯)−F(x⋆)≤ε almost surely under the output law P, for ε>0.

The optimization problem is minx∈EF(x). The norm ∥⋅∥ is induced by the inner product on E. The algorithm receives only E, m, L, and x0; the radius R and tolerance ε may enter the oracle-call budget but are not algorithm inputs.

Our assumptions:

Assumption 1 (Component convexity and smoothness). Each fi is Fréchet differentiable everywhere on E. For every i∈{0,…,m−1}, x,y∈E, and t∈[0,1], fi((1−t)x+ty)≤(1−t)fi(x)+tfi(y),∥∇fi(x)−∇fi(y)∥≤L∥x−y∥.

Assumption 2 (Interpolation and initial distance). There exists x⋆∈E such that fi(x⋆)≤fi(x)for every i∈{0,…,m−1}, x∈E,∥x0−x⋆∥≤R.

The oracle accepts any component index and any point in E and returns the exact component gradient. Our formulation is algorithm-specific: we analyze cyclic gradient descent, initialized at the given point x0. Its updates are ik=kmodm,xk+1=xk−1L∇fik(xk),k=0,1,…. Each update uses one component-gradient call. After an allotted budget of K≥0 calls, with K an integer, the output is the last iterate x¯=xK. The required accuracy is F(x¯)−F(x⋆)=1m∑i=0m−1(fi(x¯)−fi(x⋆))≤εP-a.s. The common minimizer in this requirement is fixed independently of the output; all common minimizers have the same component objective values.

theorems.referencesHtml:
• Julien Mairal. Optimization with First-Order Surrogate Functions. 2013. Complexity: O(m+mLR2/ε) fixed component-gradient calls, including initialization; MISO achieves expected average objective gap at most ε.
  • Konstantin Mishchenko, Ahmed Khaled, Peter Richtárik. Random Reshuffling: Simple Analysis with Vast Improvements. 2020. Complexity: O(m⌈LR2/ε⌉) fixed component-gradient calls under interpolation; deterministic Incremental Gradient achieves average objective gap at most ε at the average of epoch endpoints.
  • Sharan Vaswani, Francis Bach, Mark Schmidt. Fast and Faster Convergence of SGD for Over-Parameterized Models and an Accelerated Perceptron. 2019. Complexity: O(1+LR2/ε) fixed component-gradient calls under interpolation; constant-step SGD achieves expected average objective gap at most ε at an averaged output.

comparisonHtml:
On a real Hilbert space, m≥1 differentiable convex components have L-Lipschitz gradients, L>0, and a common minimizer x⋆ with ∥x0−x⋆∥≤R, R≥0. The oracle returns exact component gradients. The setup fixes cyclic gradient steps of size 1/L; the target is F(xout)−F(x⋆)≤ε, ε>0, almost surely, for the last complete-pass iterate. The guarantee holds for every outcome. Updates use m,L,x0; stopping additionally uses R,ε.

import LongTails.Template
import Mathlib.Analysis.InnerProductSpace.Basic
import Mathlib.Analysis.Calculus.Gradient.Basic
import Mathlib.Analysis.Convex.Function
import Mathlib.Algebra.Order.Floor.Ring

namespace OracleTemplate.CyclicInterpolation

def component (m : ℕ) [NeZero m] (t : ℕ) : Fin m := ⟨t % m, Nat.mod_lt _ (NeZero.pos m)⟩

noncomputable def cyclicGradient {E : Type*} [NormedAddCommGroup E] [InnerProductSpace ℝ E]
    (m : ℕ) [NeZero m] (L : ℝ) (x0 : E) : Algorithm (Fin m × E) E E where
  State := E × ℕ
  initial _ := (x0, 0)
  query s := (0, (component m s.2, s.1))
  update s reply := (s.1 - (1 / L) • reply, s.2 + 1)
  output s := s.1

end OracleTemplate.CyclicInterpolation

namespace LongTails.Setups.InterpolatedFiniteSum

open OracleTemplate OracleTemplate.CyclicInterpolation

structure Public where
  E : Type u
  [normedE : NormedAddCommGroup E]
  [linearE : InnerProductSpace ℝ E]
  [completeE : CompleteSpace E]
  m : ℕ
  [nonzero : NeZero m]
  L : ℝ
  x0 : E

attribute [instance] Public.normedE Public.linearE Public.completeE Public.nonzero

structure Params extends Public where
  R : ℝ
  ε : ℝ

abbrev spec : Setup where
  Params := Params
  Public := Public
  Instance p := Fin p.m → p.E → ℝ
  Query p := Fin p.m × p.E
  Reply p := p.E
  Output p := p.E
  publicInput := Params.toPublic
  valid q := 0 < q.L ∧ 0 ≤ q.R ∧ 0 < q.ε
  admissible q f oracle :=
    (∀ i, ConvexOn ℝ Set.univ (f i)) ∧
    (∀ k seed i x, HasGradientAt (f i) (oracle.answer k (0, (i, x)) seed) x) ∧
    (∀ k seed i x y, ‖oracle.answer k (0, (i, x)) seed - oracle.answer k (0, (i, y)) seed‖ ≤ q.L * ‖x - y‖) ∧
    (∃ xstar, (∀ i, IsMinOn (f i) Set.univ xstar) ∧ ‖q.x0 - xstar‖ ≤ q.R)
  successful q f output P :=
    ∃ xstar, (∀ i, IsMinOn (f i) Set.univ xstar) ∧
      ∀ᵐ ω ∂(P : MeasureTheory.Measure _),
        (q.m : ℝ)⁻¹ * ∑ i, (f i (output ω) - f i xstar) ≤ q.ε
  allowedAlgorithm p algorithm := algorithm = cyclicGradient p.m p.L p.x0

end LongTails.Setups.InterpolatedFiniteSum
